one_liner: National on-the-record DOJ spokesperson who handles press inquiries, writes releases and talking points, and coordinates press events for DOJ components and U.S. Attorneys' Offices.
fit_summary: GS-11 requires a year at GS-9 level covering all three areas: public relations programs, research for media inquiries and drafting releases or talking points. Daniel's resume shows writing (proposals, minutes, client documents) but no public information or media work, so qualifying will be hard.
eligibility: Hiring paths listed are public and fed-transition, so U.S. citizens without federal status like Daniel may apply.

GS-11 requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-09 that includes all three areas: assisting with public relations programs, researching responses to media inquiries, and drafting news releases, fact sheets, or talking points.

GS-12 requires one year equivalent to GS-11 that includes advising decision-makers on public affairs, representing an organization in media interviews or press conferences, and responding to news media inquiries.
The education alternative for GS-11 is a Ph.D., 3 years of graduate study, or an LL.M. (or a qualifying combination of education and experience); you must meet all requirements by 11/05/2026.
No security clearance is required, but expect a background investigation for a DOJ position.
strategy: Apply at GS-11 only if he can show public relations or media work, paid or volunteer, that isn't on his resume yet.

Describe your IEM work in the posting's three specialized-experience terms if it truly included them, for example disaster public information messaging, research for client or media questions, and drafting fact sheets or talking points.

Within your two-page limit, list dates, hours per week, and titles for every job, and use the exact phrases 'news releases, fact sheets, informational pieces, or talking points' where they are accurate.
Preview the questionnaire at the posted USA Staffing link before applying, and rate yourself 'expert' only where a resume bullet backs it up, since inflated answers can get you excluded.
The window is very short (10/30 to 11/05/2026), so have your resume ready in advance and block time to finish the USA Hire assessment within 48 hours after closing.
If you lack direct press experience, also apply to GS-7/9 public affairs or communications roles and to legislative press assistant jobs to build the required year.
resume_bullets: Led proposal writing for multimillion-dollar government bids (2019–2024).
Answered homeowners' questions at a five-person ReBuild NC intake center after Hurricane Matthew (2019).
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you had to respond quickly to a media inquiry on a sensitive issue. What steps did you take?
How would you align messaging between a U.S. Attorney's Office and DOJ headquarters when the two have different priorities?
Describe a news release or set of talking points you drafted. How did you make sure it was accurate and cleared?
How do you build and maintain relationships with reporters while protecting information that isn't public?
watch_outs: The application window is only about one week, and the USA Hire assessment is due within 48 hours after the posting closes.
All three specialized-experience elements are required; general policy knowledge or emergency-management operations work without communications duties will likely be rated ineligible.
As a national on-the-record spokesperson for law enforcement matters, you will work under high pressure with strict discretion and may need to be available after hours.
Veterans' preference eligibles get selection priority within each category, which lowers the odds for non-veterans.
